string.name: feature_guide_intro
string.value: Tap a feature to view its setup steps and checks. Most options use a switch; policy examples are only needed for advanced remote sharing. MeshArc does not change your tailnet policy for you. Never replace an existing policy with an example; ask your administrator if unsure.

string.name: feature_guide_policy_hint
string.value: Read-only policy example: replace the identity and merge into existing arrays. Long-press → Select all → Copy. Only the docs share on your own untagged devices is allowed.

string.name: feature_guide_commands_hint
string.value: Run on the remote computer, not on this phone. Replace the sample folder/subnet first. Long-press and copy only the command for your platform, not the headings or other platforms.

string.name: feature_guide_connect_body
string.value:
1. Install Tailscale on your computer, NAS or server and join the same tailnet.
2. Sign in with MeshArc, connect and allow the system VPN request.
3. Select an online device on Home and copy its Tailscale IP (usually 100.x.x.x) into the service client.
Check: both devices are online and the remote service is running. No config editing is needed.
If unavailable: disconnect other system VPNs and ask an admin to approve the device in Machines if required. The Use MagicDNS switch is on by default. If MagicDNS is enabled on your tailnet, copy the device name from its details; otherwise, use its IP address. Reconnect manually after a restart.

string.name: feature_guide_taildrop_body
string.value:
Enable in the Tailscale admin console → Settings → General → Send Files (Taildrop).
1. An Owner or Admin enables Send Files; no policy editing is required.
2. Connect both devices with the same user account and run a Taildrop-capable receiver. Tagged devices and devices shared by another user are not personal Taildrop targets.
3. In MeshArc Transfer (MeshSend), select a Taildrop-ready device and choose files or photos. Save received items to Files or Photos when prompted.
Check: the target is Taildrop-ready and a small file arrives.
If unavailable: check the switch, device ownership, online status and receiver version. LocalSend availability does not imply Taildrop availability.
Platform note: first-time macOS use also requires Tailscale in System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Sharing. Follow the official Taildrop guide for Linux/NAS file retrieval.

string.name: feature_guide_taildrive_body
string.value:
Taildrive is separate from Taildrop: it needs policy authorization and a folder shared by a computer. MeshArc accesses remote shares; it does not publish phone folders. The official feature remains alpha.
1. Ask an Owner, Admin or Network admin to open Access controls. Prefer the visual editor: add drive:share and drive:access under Node attributes for your user, then a tailscale.com/cap/drive application grant.
2. The example below is read-only. Replace you@example.com with your actual policy identity. It permits only that user to read shares on their own untagged devices. If the visual editor cannot express the application grant, use JSON editor.
3. Preserve your existing policy. Append the sample objects to existing nodeAttrs and grants arrays, creating an array only if absent. Do not replace the whole policy, duplicate top-level keys or change source/destination to *. Validate and save. Ask your administrator if you lack edit access.
4. Share a folder on a Windows, macOS or Linux computer running Tailscale 1.64.0+. Replace the sample path with an existing folder. Run the command on that computer, not on your phone or in the admin console.
5. Connect MeshArc, refresh Files and open the device → share.
Check: docs and its files appear. Write actions are intentionally denied by the read-only example; ask an admin to change that grant from ro to rw only if writing is needed.
If unavailable: check the published share, both node attributes, application grant and OS folder permissions. Tagged NAS devices and cross-user sharing need a separate policy.
Computer tip: create the folder first in your file manager. If tailscale is not found, check the client installation and CLI path; macOS can also expose File Sharing settings as documented, choose a shared folder and name the share docs.

string.name: feature_guide_localsend_body
string.value:
1. Open LocalSend or a compatible receiver such as JieChuan, keep its receiving service running and allow network access. No Taildrop switch or Taildrive policy is required.
2. For remote transfers, connect both devices to the same tailnet and allow the receiver service in its policy. On a LAN, permit discovery and the receiving port.
3. Check LocalSend status in MeshArc Transfer, select an available target and choose LocalSend if both protocols are offered.
4. Accept on the receiving device. If its port was changed, enter the actual value in the target port settings (commonly 53317 by default).
Check: LocalSend is available and a file arrives.
If unavailable: check the running receiver, firewall, network permission and port. Its status and switches are independent of Taildrop.

string.name: feature_guide_exit_title
string.value: Exit nodes · use a remote connection

string.name: feature_guide_exit_body
string.value:
1. Connect the intended exit computer to Tailscale. Prefer Run exit node in Windows/macOS clients. On Linux, enable IP forwarding as documented before running the command below.
2. An admin approves Use as exit node under Machines → Edit route settings and verifies your policy permits using it. Approval alone is not sufficient.
3. In MeshArc Settings → Network & connection, select the exit node. Enable local network access if you also need your current LAN. Disconnect and reconnect if the UI requests it.
Check: the selected exit works as intended; select no exit node to restore normal routing.
If unavailable: check the node, approval, policy, IP forwarding and firewall. MeshArc uses remote exits; it does not advertise your phone as one.

string.name: feature_guide_subnet_body
string.value:
1. Install Tailscale on a computer/NAS that can reach the destination LAN and enable IP forwarding following its platform guide.
2. Replace the example 192.168.1.0/24 with your actual destination subnet. Advertise from that router, preserving the full existing route list.
3. An admin approves the subnet in Machines → router → Edit route settings and allows your user to reach the required destination IPs and ports.
4. Enable Accept subnet routes in MeshArc Settings → Network & connection, connect and use the LAN device’s original IP.
Check: an authorized LAN service is reachable.
If unavailable: check overlapping subnets, approval, policy, forwarding and the target firewall. LAN devices do not each need Tailscale, but approval does not grant unrestricted LAN access.

string.name: feature_guide_media_body
string.value:
1. Install and start Jellyfin, Emby or Plex on a computer/NAS and verify its library and account locally.
2. Connect the server and phone to the same tailnet. Check listening addresses, actual ports and firewall; a localhost-only service is not remotely accessible. Taildrop/Taildrive permissions are unrelated.
3. Install a compatible HosPlayer, select a discovered media service in MeshArc device details and open the player. Sign in to your media account there.
Check: a library opens and a test video plays.
If unavailable: check the Tailscale IP, port, service type and access policy. MeshArc does not install a media server or enter media passwords for you.

string.name: feature_guide_streaming_body
string.value:
1. Install and configure Sunshine on the computer and verify its games and encoder locally.
2. Connect both ends to the tailnet and permit Sunshine’s required ports. Use a compatible Moonlight client on the phone, add the computer’s Tailscale IP and complete PIN pairing.
Check: a real streaming session succeeds; an online device or successful Sunshine probe is not proof of streaming.
One-tap streaming requires a MoonlightOH build supporting the MeshArc launch contract. With older builds, copy the host address and add it manually. Existing hosts are reused by UUID with pairing preserved. Direct connections retain the user bitrate limit; relay sessions use lower limits with adaptive bitrate. The prompt also allows keeping the original configuration.

string.name: feature_guide_security_body
string.value:
1. Configure a screen lock or biometrics in system settings.
2. In MeshArc Settings → Security, enable app lock or Taildrive folder lock and complete system authentication.
3. Authenticate when entering protected content again; follow the UI authentication requirement when disabling protection.
Check: protected content triggers system authentication. No config editing is needed.
This protects access through MeshArc on this device. It is not file encryption and does not change remote permissions; server and tailnet policy still govern reading and writing.

string.name: feature_guide_appearance_body
string.value:
Open MeshArc Settings → Appearance & navigation / Storage & cache.
1. Adjust background, immersive material and animation directly in the UI. No config is needed.
2. Inspect storage usage and clear temporary cache only when related transfers or previews are inactive.
Check: settings take effect in the UI; some material effects require device support.
Appearance settings do not enable network features or change permissions. Clearing local temporary cache does not delete remote Taildrive files.
